title: Edge-to-edge, insets & large screens
scopeHtml: Scope: edge-to-edge enforcement, WindowInsets (Compose and Views), system bars, window size classes, adaptive layouts, foldables, multi-window, Android 16 large-screen rules, predictive back UI, resizable testing, Chromebook input.

questions.promptHtml: What exactly changed for your app when you bumped targetSdk to 35, and what do you call in onCreate to make behaviour consistent on older OS versions?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Every Play app hit this in 2025. They want to know you understand it is a targetSdk-gated behaviour change, not an "Android 15 only" thing.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: "On Android 15+, if targetSdk is 35 or higher, the system forces the window to draw edge-to-edge: behind the status bar, navigation bar and display cutout. Anything I used to rely on being outside the bars (the content frame) is now under them, so I must apply insets as padding myself. enableEdgeToEdge() from androidx.activity makes API 21+ behave the same way, so I don't have a split behaviour between OS versions. The windowOptOutEdgeToEdgeEnforcement opt-out is a temporary escape hatch and does not work once targeting 36 (verify in the current docs)."

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html:
Before: the decor view fitted content inside the system bar insets (the app window did not overlap the bars). After: the app window spans the whole screen; bars are transparent overlays (3-button nav gets a translucent scrim; gesture nav is fully transparent). The system no longer lets you set statusBarColor / navigationBarColor meaningfully when targeting 35 (deprecated, no effect). Contrast is handled by the system (scrim for 3-button nav) and by you through light/dark icon appearance.

targetSdk <= 34         targetSdk >= 35 (Android 15+)
+---------------+       +---------------+
| status bar    |       |  content      |  <- content under bars
+---------------+       |  (draws       |
|  content      |       |   behind      |
+---------------+       |   everything) |
| nav bar       |       +---------------+
+---------------+

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
class MainActivity : ComponentActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        enableEdgeToEdge() // call BEFORE super.onCreate / setContent per docs guidance
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        setContent { AppTheme { AppRoot() } }
    }
}

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Thinking enforcement hits only devices on Android 15: it is Android 15+ AND targetSdk >= 35. An Android 16 device with a targetSdk 34 app is not forced.
  • Still calling window.statusBarColor = ... and expecting it to work.
  • Fixing only Scaffold screens and forgetting dialogs, bottom sheets, full-screen Dialogs and AndroidView fragments.
  • Testing only on gesture nav: 3-button nav adds a scrim and a different bottom inset.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Does enableEdgeToEdge() consume insets for me? → No. It only configures the window and bar styling; you still apply insets.
  2. Why is bottom content under a button bar on one device only? → That device uses 3-button nav (larger bottom inset) or has a taller IME/cutout; hardcoded dp padding was hiding it.
  3. Why call before setContent? → It sets decor/window flags and bar styles; the first frame must already be edge-to-edge or you get a flash/relayout.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE: "the app now draws behind the bars, add padding." Senior: knows the targetSdk gate, the deprecated bar colors, Material components that already handle insets vs those (AppBarLayout, custom views, dialogs) that do not, and plans a device matrix test (gesture, 3-button, cutout, tablet).

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: After a targetSdk bump, a payments app's "Pay" button sat under the gesture bar on 3-button devices; support tickets spiked while internal QA (gesture nav only) saw nothing.

questions.promptHtml: What are the main WindowInsets types in Compose, and when would you pick safeDrawing over systemBars?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Picking the wrong inset type is the most common source of clipped UI.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: "systemBars is status bar plus navigation bar plus caption bar. displayCutout is the notch. ime is the keyboard. safeDrawing is the union of systemBars, ime and displayCutout: everything where I should not put anything I need the user to read or tap. safeGestures avoids system gesture zones for things like carousels or sliders. safeContent is safeDrawing plus safeGestures. For normal screen content I use safeDrawing or let Scaffold handle it."

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html:
Compose exposes WindowInsets.Companion properties backed by WindowInsetsCompat from the root view. Each is a live State-like object: reading it in layout/draw phase does not recompose when the keyboard animates if you use windowInsetsPadding (which reads in the layout phase). statusBars.asPaddingValues() reads in composition and will recompose each animation frame for the IME: prefer modifiers.

Type Contains Use for
statusBars top bar top app bar background
navigationBars bottom/side nav bottom bar
systemBars status + nav + caption most chrome
displayCutout notch/hole-punch landscape side padding
ime keyboard text input screens
safeDrawing systemBars + ime + cutout default content padding
safeGestures gesture zones edge-sensitive widgets
tappableElement 3-button nav, not gesture bar buttons you must tap

sections.label: Code
sections.html: Box(Modifier.fillMaxSize().windowInsetsPadding(WindowInsets.safeDrawing)) { Content() }

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Using statusBars alone: ignores the notch in landscape (side cutout).
  • Using systemBars on a form: keyboard still covers fields.
  • Using asPaddingValues() for IME: recomposes on every animation frame.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Difference between navigationBars and tappableElement? → In gesture nav the bar is not tappable, so tappableElement inset is ~0 and you may draw under it while still avoiding 3-button bars.
  2. Is safeDrawing enough for a full-screen map? → No, draw the map behind, and apply insets only to controls.
  3. How do you read inset in dp? → WindowInsets.safeDrawing.asPaddingValues() or getBottom(density) inside Modifier.layout/onSizeChanged lambda to avoid recomposition.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE names status/navigation bars. Senior distinguishes draw vs gesture vs tappable insets and knows reading insets in composition vs layout phase cost.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A video app's seek bar sat in the gesture-back zone; users swiped back instead of scrubbing, until safeGestures padding was applied.

questions.promptHtml: What are window size classes, what are the breakpoints, and why not just check isTablet?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Tests whether you think in window size (resizable, split-screen) not device type.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: "A window size class buckets the current window (not the screen) by width and height: width Compact < 600dp, Medium 600 to < 840dp, Expanded >= 840dp; height Compact < 480dp, Medium 480 to < 900dp, Expanded >= 900dp. Larger classes (Large, Extra-large width) were added in later adaptive releases (verify exact values and names in your adaptive version). It is based on window bounds, so split-screen, freeform on Chromebook, and fold/unfold all change it at runtime. isTablet is a device property that lies the moment a tablet is in a half-screen window."

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Compute from WindowMetrics (currentWindowAdaptiveInfo() in androidx.compose.material3.adaptive; older: calculateWindowSizeClass(activity) from material3-window-size-class). Use width class for layout structure (nav rail vs bottom bar, one vs two panes) and height class for vertical affordances (landscape phones are Compact height). Treat classes as a coarse switch; inside a class use BoxWithConstraints/flexible layouts. Recomputes on configuration/window-bounds change without Activity recreation if configChanges covers it (see Q347).

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
@Composable
fun Root() {
    val info = currentWindowAdaptiveInfo()
    val wsc = info.windowSizeClass
    if (wsc.isWidthAtLeastBreakpoint(WindowSizeClass.WIDTH_DP_MEDIUM_LOWER_BOUND)) TwoPane() else OnePane()
}

(isWidthAtLeastBreakpoint exists in newer adaptive versions; on older ones use windowSizeClass.windowWidthSizeClass == WindowWidthSizeClass.COMPACT: verify against your version.)

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Using LocalConfiguration.current.screenWidthDp (screen-ish, not window in some modes).
  • Using height Compact as "phone": a landscape phone and a short split pane both qualify.
  • Passing WindowSizeClass down 8 layers: read currentWindowAdaptiveInfo() where needed.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Can a phone be Expanded? → Unfolded foldable inner display in portrait often is Medium/Expanded, yes.
  2. Why is there flicker on rotation? → Class changed and state keyed to class got reset; hoist state above the switch.
  3. Where do you use ranges finer than classes? → Content grids with GridCells.Adaptive(minSize).

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE: "compact/medium/expanded." Senior: window not device, width for structure/height for affordances, state hoisting across class changes.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: An app gated tablet UI by smallestScreenWidthDp; ChromeOS freeform windows at 400dp wide got a broken tablet layout.

questions.promptHtml: Explain how insets propagate and get consumed in Compose. When do you need consumeWindowInsets?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Double padding is the classic edge-to-edge bug.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: "Insets flow down the tree via modifiers. windowInsetsPadding(x) applies the part of x not yet consumed by ancestors, then marks it consumed for descendants. consumeWindowInsets(x) marks inset as consumed without adding padding, for when padding came from somewhere else, like Scaffold's innerPadding. Without consuming, a child's imePadding() or safeDrawing padding adds the same space a second time."

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html:
Each insets modifier maintains an InsetsConsumed-style node: the unconsumed insets of the parent are passed to child modifier nodes via a modifier-local. windowInsetsPadding computes padding = inset - alreadyConsumed (per side, clamped at 0) and then adds its own to the consumed set. So nesting systemBars padding twice is safe (second sees consumed = full, adds 0). It is unsafe when the padding was added by plain padding() with values derived from insets, since the modifier-local does not know.

Scaffold(contentWindowInsets = safeDrawing)
 -> innerPadding = top 48dp (bar), bottom 24dp (nav)
 -> content: Modifier.padding(innerPadding)        // padding added, NOT marked consumed
      .consumeWindowInsets(innerPadding)           // mark consumed
        .imePadding()                              // now only the keyboard part beyond 24dp

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
Scaffold { inner ->
    LazyColumn(
        Modifier.padding(inner).consumeWindowInsets(inner).imePadding()
    ) { /* ... */ }
}

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Modifier.padding(inner).imePadding() without consume: IME padding adds the nav-bar height again (a visible gap).
  • Placing consumeWindowInsets after the child that needs it: modifier order matters; it affects only what is below it.
  • Consuming too much so later windowInsetsPadding returns 0 and content hides under bars.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. consumeWindowInsets vs windowInsetsPadding? → consume = mark only; padding = apply + mark.
  2. What does Scaffold do by default? → Applies contentWindowInsets (systemBars-ish, excluding IME) to the inner padding it hands you, and consumes them for the content slot (verify per Material3 version).
  3. How is this different in Views? → View dispatch is a pass-through of WindowInsets where a view returns modified/consumed insets to stop children; Compose models it with modifiers (Q342).

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE knows imePadding. Senior explains per-side subtraction, modifier ordering, and that padding(innerPadding) does not consume.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: Chat screen had a ~48dp blank band above the keyboard on gesture-nav phones: nav bar inset applied twice.

questions.promptHtml: With edge-to-edge on, how does the keyboard resize your layout? What happened to adjustResize?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: The old resize contract silently changed; many teams broke forms.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: "With edge-to-edge the window is not resized for the keyboard by default in the way fitsSystemWindows apps relied on. The keyboard is delivered as WindowInsets.ime, and I apply it with imePadding() or windowInsetsPadding(WindowInsets.ime). adjustResize in the manifest is still the mode I want (so the IME insets are reported and animated on API 30+), but I own the layout response. On API 30+ the insets are animated, on older versions they jump."

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: WindowInsetsAnimation (API 30+, backported partially via WindowInsetsCompat and ViewCompat.setWindowInsetsAnimationCallback, with adjustResize on older versions) reports IME progress each frame; Compose's ime inset reads it so imePadding() follows the keyboard animation smoothly in the layout phase, no recomposition. Use WindowInsets.isImeVisible (experimental in some versions: verify) to react to visibility. For scrollable forms: padding plus bringIntoViewRequester / Modifier.imeNestedScroll() to scroll content with the keyboard.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
Column(
    Modifier.fillMaxSize()
        .safeDrawingPadding()     // includes ime
        .verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())
) { OutlinedTextField(/* ... */); Button(/* ... */) }

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• android:windowSoftInputMode="adjustPan" plus edge-to-edge: window pans, insets still reported, content jumps oddly.
  • Applying imePadding on each field inside a column: stacked/cumulative paddings unless consumed.
  • Forgetting a Dialog's own window: it needs decorFitsSystemWindows = false handling or its own insets.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Why does the layout jump on API 29? → no animation API; resize is a single step.
  2. Keep bottom CTA above keyboard? → Modifier.imePadding() on the bottom bar, with Scaffold insets consumed.
  3. imeNestedScroll? → Lets dragging a scroller down dismiss/animate the keyboard (Compose foundation modifier; verify version).

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE: "add imePadding." Senior: explains animated insets, adjustResize still needed for reporting, the consume interaction, and dialog/window-per-popup caveats.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: Checkout form's "Place order" was hidden by the keyboard on one OEM that ignored adjustResize for dialogs.

questions.promptHtml: How do you handle insets in a View-based screen (XML/Fragment), and what does returning CONSUMED do?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Many large apps are mixed Views/Compose; interviewers probe real migration knowledge.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: "I use ViewCompat.setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener(view), read insets.getInsets(WindowInsetsCompat.Type.systemBars() or displayCutout()), apply them as padding or margin, and return either the insets (so children also see them) or WindowInsetsCompat.CONSUMED (so the subtree doesn't). fitsSystemWindows=true is the legacy shortcut that pads by system bars. In a hierarchy, insets dispatch parent to child, first-listener-wins unless you pass them on."

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: View.dispatchApplyWindowInsets calls the listener or onApplyWindowInsets, then (for ViewGroups) passes the result to each child until one consumes. Since API 30 insets are dispatched to all children regardless of consumption unless the parent sets compat behavior (WindowInsetsCompat papers over this; verify). Cache initial padding so repeated dispatches do not accumulate: capture original padding once, then set initial + inset.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
val initial = Insets.of(v.paddingLeft, v.paddingTop, v.paddingRight, v.paddingBottom)
ViewCompat.setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener(v) { view, windowInsets ->
    val bars = windowInsets.getInsets(
        WindowInsetsCompat.Type.systemBars() or WindowInsetsCompat.Type.displayCutout()
    )
    view.updatePadding(bars.left + initial.left, bars.top + initial.top, bars.right + initial.right, bars.bottom + initial.bottom)
    WindowInsetsCompat.CONSUMED
}

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Reading paddingBottom on every dispatch and adding inset: padding grows each time.
  • Returning CONSUMED from the root and wondering why a child AppBarLayout or RecyclerView can't pad itself.
  • clipToPadding=true on a RecyclerView: content can't scroll under the nav bar; set clipToPadding=false.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. fitsSystemWindows pitfalls? → Applies to the first view that consumes; behaves differently by container and breaks with edge-to-edge custom layouts.
  2. Fragment containers? → Each fragment's root can register its own listener; call ViewCompat.requestApplyInsets after attaching.
  3. ComposeView inside a View hierarchy? → Compose reads insets from the host view's last dispatched insets; consuming above it zeros Compose's insets (check ViewCompat.setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener ordering).

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE: fitsSystemWindows. Senior: listener pattern with initial padding capture, clipToPadding, consumption semantics, and Compose interop effects.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A hybrid screen showed zero IME padding in its ComposeView because the host Fragment root returned CONSUMED.

questions.promptHtml: How do you control status/navigation bar icon colors and contrast now that bar colors are gone?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Unreadable white-on-white status icons are an easy-to-ship regression.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: "Bars are transparent; I choose icon tint (light or dark icons) to match what's behind them. enableEdgeToEdge(statusBarStyle = SystemBarStyle.auto(lightScrim, darkScrim), navigationBarStyle = ...) auto-picks by system dark mode. For per-screen control I use WindowCompat.getInsetsController(window, view).isAppearanceLightStatusBars. For 3-button nav the system adds a scrim, controllable with window.isNavigationBarContrastEnforced, which is API 29+."

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Icon appearance is a window attribute (not per-view). If the top of the screen is an image (dark) on a light theme, set light-icons false while that screen is resumed, restore on dispose. Do this in a DisposableEffect, not by mutating in composition. SystemBarStyle.auto and .dark/.light are androidx.activity APIs.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
@Composable
fun StatusBarIcons(light: Boolean) {
    val view = LocalView.current
    DisposableEffect(light) {
        val c = WindowCompat.getInsetsController((view.context as Activity).window, view)
        val old = c.isAppearanceLightStatusBars
        c.isAppearanceLightStatusBars = light
        onDispose { c.isAppearanceLightStatusBars = old }
    }
}

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Setting appearance inside composition body (side effect on every recomposition).
  • Casting view.context to Activity when it's a ContextWrapper: unwrap with a loop.
  • Ignoring the nav scrim, drawing a bright footer under dark 3-button icons.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Why did my statusBarColor stop working? → Deprecated/no effect on target 35.
  2. Two screens in a NavHost with different icon needs? → Key the effect on route and restore on dispose; mind transition overlap.
  3. Dark theme toggle at runtime? → Activity is recreated unless uiMode is handled; SystemBarStyle.auto reevaluates on recreation.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE flips a boolean. Senior handles lifecycle/restoration, contrast enforcement, and navigation overlap.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: Hero-image screens left white status icons over a white toolbar after back navigation because the old value was never restored.

questions.promptHtml: What does NavigationSuiteScaffold do, and when would you not use it?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Checks adaptive navigation knowledge and judgment about prebuilt components.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: "It picks the navigation component from window size class: bottom NavigationBar for compact, NavigationRail for medium, and permanent/wide drawer or rail for expanded, via NavigationSuiteScaffoldDefaults.calculateFromAdaptiveInfo. I declare items once with item(...) in its content lambda. I skip it if I need a custom bar (floating, animated, central FAB cutout) or per-destination nav layouts, where I would write the switch by hand using the same window info."

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Artifact androidx.compose.material3:material3-adaptive-navigation-suite (verify version). Layout type is derived from WindowAdaptiveInfo (window size class + posture). Overrides: layoutType = ... param, e.g. force bottom bar in tabletop posture on a fold (default behaviour shows rail on tabletop? verify) or hide nav in immersive modes. The scaffold itself handles insets for the nav component, you handle insets of content via the lambda.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
var current by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(Dest.Home) }
NavigationSuiteScaffold(
    navigationSuiteItems = {
        Dest.entries.forEach { d ->
            item(selected = d == current, onClick = { current = d },
                icon = { Icon(d.icon, null) }, label = { Text(d.label) })
        }
    }
) { Content(current) }

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Holding current in remember not rememberSaveable/ViewModel: lost on rotation/fold.
  • Nesting a second Scaffold bottom bar, ending up with two bars.
  • Not providing content descriptions for rail items, which show icon-only.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. How do you force a layout? → layoutType argument, computed from your own rule.
  2. Hide it in full-screen detail? → Use NavigationSuiteType.None.
  3. How does it interact with predictive back and Navigation? → Destination state lives in your NavController; suite is just chrome.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE: "switches bottom bar to rail." Senior: explains how it derives from adaptive info/posture, overrides, state ownership, and limits.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A team double-stacked bars on tablets by wrapping the suite around screens that still had their own bottom Scaffold.

questions.promptHtml: How does ListDetailPaneScaffold work, and how do you get correct back behaviour between one-pane and two-pane modes?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Canonical layout implementation; back/state across size transitions is where bugs live.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: "A scaffold gets a directive (computed from window size/posture: how many panes, spacing) and a value (which panes are shown right now). rememberListDetailPaneScaffoldNavigator<T>() manages a pane history. On compact it shows one pane, navigateTo(Detail, item) swaps to detail and navigateBack() pops. On expanded both show, so navigateTo only changes the detail selection and back has nothing to pop. I wire BackHandler/PredictiveBackHandler-friendly navigator.navigateBack() and keep the selected id in saveable state."

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Scaffold role roles: List, Detail, Extra. ThreePaneScaffoldNavigator keeps a back stack of destinations (pane + content key). The PaneScaffoldDirective defines max horizontal partitions and gaps; default hides panes that don't fit (HidePane strategy). scaffoldValue[role] is Expanded or Hidden. Because the navigator state is saveable, rotation/fold changes re-evaluate the value from the same stack, so the user keeps their selection. Medium width defaults to one pane in some versions: customize the directive (verify in release notes).

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
val navigator = rememberListDetailPaneScaffoldNavigator<Long>()
BackHandler(navigator.canNavigateBack()) { navigator.navigateBack() }
ListDetailPaneScaffold(
    directive = navigator.scaffoldDirective,
    value = navigator.scaffoldValue,
    listPane = { AnimatedPane { Inbox(onClick = { navigator.navigateTo(ListDetailPaneScaffoldRole.Detail, it) }) } },
    detailPane = { AnimatedPane { navigator.currentDestination?.contentKey?.let { Detail(it) } } }
)

(navigateTo is suspend in newer versions: call in a coroutine; verify.)

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Keeping the selected item in remember not saved: fold/unfold resets it.
  • Back with two panes showing pops the list or exits unexpectedly: use canNavigateBack as the enabled flag.
  • Loading detail data on navigateTo instead of keying a ViewModel by the content key: refetch on every size change.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Where does the Navigation component fit? → Put the scaffold inside one destination, or use the navigator as state and sync via nav args; do not duplicate back stacks.
  2. Three panes (supporting pane)? → SupportingPaneScaffold / extra pane role.
  3. Shared element/animation between panes? → AnimatedPane plus shared element APIs where supported (verify).

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE: copy sample. Senior: reasons about directive vs value, back-stack semantics when panes become visible, saved state and ViewModel keying.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: An email client lost the open message on unfold because selection lived in remember.

questions.promptHtml: How do you make an app fold-aware? Explain tabletop and book postures and how you read them.

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Separates people who've shipped for foldables from those who only resize.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: "I collect WindowInfoTracker.getOrCreate(context).windowLayoutInfo(activity) as a Flow in a lifecycle-aware way, find a FoldingFeature in displayFeatures, and check state (FLAT or HALF_OPENED), orientation (HORIZONTAL or VERTICAL), isSeparating and occlusionType. Tabletop = HALF_OPENED + HORIZONTAL fold; book = HALF_OPENED + VERTICAL. In tabletop I place content above the fold and controls below, using the fold bounds as the split, not a hardcoded 50%."

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: WindowManager is the only stable cross-OEM API. The feature gives bounds in window coordinates. A hinge with occlusionType = FULL hides pixels: keep content out of it. isSeparating tells you whether to treat the halves as separate panes (also what adaptive scaffolds use for posture-aware directives). Capability check: supportedPostures on newer WindowManager (verify version). Don't assume fold means size class change: half-open on some devices keeps the same window.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
@Composable
fun rememberTabletop(activity: Activity): State<Boolean> {
    val flow = remember(activity) {
        WindowInfoTracker.getOrCreate(activity).windowLayoutInfo(activity)
            .map { info -> info.displayFeatures.filterIsInstance<FoldingFeature>().any {
                it.state == FoldingFeature.State.HALF_OPENED &&
                it.orientation == FoldingFeature.Orientation.HORIZONTAL } }
    }
    return flow.collectAsStateWithLifecycle(false)
}

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Collecting with collectAsState (not lifecycle-aware) so work continues when stopped.
  • Handling unfold by Activity restart: state loss (see Q353).
  • Testing only the emulator's foldable skins and skipping real hinge occlusion.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. How do you test without a device? → Android Studio foldable emulators with virtual sensors; WindowLayoutInfoPublisherRule / TestWindowLayoutInfo in androidx.window:window-testing.
  2. Flex mode on Samsung? → Reported via WindowManager as HALF_OPENED horizontal.
  3. Dual-screen? → Same FoldingFeature with isSeparating = true and a non-zero hinge.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE: "use WindowManager." Senior: uses fold bounds, handles occlusion, lifecycle-aware flows, and a posture-aware fallback for non-fold devices.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A video-call app's controls hid in the hinge on one dual-screen device because it split at 50% of the window.

questions.promptHtml: What changes for your Activity in multi-window mode, and how do you handle configuration changes from resizing?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Multi-window breaks assumptions about "visible implies resumed" and about config change cost.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: "Since Android 10 (API 29) every visible activity in multi-window is RESUMED; only one is the top-resumed one, reported via onTopResumedActivityChanged. Before 10, the non-focused window was only PAUSED. Resizing triggers a configuration change (screenSize, smallestScreenSize, screenLayout, orientation). By default the Activity is recreated, so state must survive via ViewModel and saved state. Declaring configChanges avoids recreation but then I must react in onConfigurationChanged/Compose recomposition myself."

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Compose handles size changes by recomposing with new LocalConfiguration/window metrics if the activity declares android:configChanges="orientation|screenSize|smallestScreenSize|screenLayout|keyboardHidden" (ComponentActivity-based Compose apps commonly do). Costs without it: process-intact recreation (~100s of ms, camera/media reopen). Don't pause video on onPause in multi-window: the app is still visible. Use onStop for pause of media unless in PiP.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
<activity android:name=".MainActivity"
    android:resizeableActivity="true"
    android:configChanges="orientation|screenSize|smallestScreenSize|screenLayout|density|keyboard|keyboardHidden|navigation" />

(Compose docs recommend this set for resizable apps; verify against current guidance.)

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Pausing playback or camera in onPause: wrong in multi-window.
  • resizeableActivity="false" on tablets: compat mode letterboxing (and under Android 16 rules on large screens it's ignored for target 36, see Q348).
  • Assuming onResume implies input focus; use onTopResumedActivityChanged or Window focus callbacks.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Does configChanges handle every case? → Not for locale/uiMode unless listed; recreation still occurs otherwise.
  2. How to support two instances of the same Activity? → FLAG_ACTIVITY_MULTIPLE_TASK/documentLaunchMode / allowMultipleInstances semantics (verify).
  3. Drag and drop between windows? → DragAndDropTarget/dragAndDropTarget modifier and ClipData with URI permission flags.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE: "state in ViewModel." Senior adds all-resumed since API 29, media lifecycle choices, configChanges cost trade-offs.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A video app paused on every split-screen focus switch because pause lived in onPause; reviews called it "broken on tablets".

questions.promptHtml: What does Android 16 change for apps that lock orientation or declare non-resizable on large screens, and how do you prepare?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Current, version-specific, and affects Play review/visibility.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: "For apps targeting API 36 running on displays with smallest width >= 600dp, the system ignores screenOrientation, resizeableActivity=false, minAspectRatio, maxAspectRatio and setRequestedOrientation(). Games (by appCategory) and users who opt in through the aspect-ratio setting are exempt. For API 36 you can temporarily opt out with android.window.PROPERTY_COMPAT_ALLOW_RESTRICTED_RESIZABILITY (app or activity level); Google's table shows that opt-out going away at API 37 (verify). So I need layouts that survive any size and orientation."

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Source: Android Developers blog "Orientation and resizability changes in Android 16" and the Android 16 behavior-changes page. Consequences: portrait-locked camera/scanner UIs now run in landscape and any window shape; code that did requestedOrientation = SCREEN_ORIENTATION_PORTRAIT is a no-op on those displays; code assuming Display.rotation equals UI orientation breaks. Preparation checklist: remove manifest locks or gate them by size class, test with resizable emulator, make camera preview use Display/window metrics to rotate correctly, check hardcoded aspect ratios, test minAspectRatio assumptions, state restoration on resize.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
<!-- temporary, API 36 only: verify property placement per docs -->
<property android:name="android.window.PROPERTY_COMPAT_ALLOW_RESTRICTED_RESIZABILITY"
          android:value="true" />

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Treating opt-out as a plan: it expires (API 37 table).
  • Only testing phones: restriction applies to sw >= 600dp, not phones.
  • Using the opt-out to hide layout bugs, then Play large-screen quality tier suffers.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Which API level applies the change? → App targetSdk 36 on Android 16 (verify rollout).
  2. What replaces a hard portrait lock for a scanner? → Adaptive layout plus camera preview transform from window rotation; keep lock only for phones via a size-class check at runtime (still not the manifest).
  3. Impact on games? → Exempt via android:appCategory="game".

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE: "make it responsive." Senior: knows exact attributes ignored, exemptions, opt-out sunset, and camera/sensor assumptions that break.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A portrait-only banking app lost its OTP-field focus handling in landscape tablets because the layout used fixed heights.

questions.promptHtml: How do you support predictive back in a Compose app, and what UI has to change?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Tests lifecycle of the back gesture and API migration awareness.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: "Predictive back shows a preview animation while the user drags back. To opt in I set android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true" (application or activity) and migrate from onBackPressed()/KeyEvent to OnBackPressedCallback or Compose BackHandler/PredictiveBackHandler. PredictiveBackHandler gives a Flow<BackEventCompat> with progress so I can animate, then commit or cancel. System animations (back-to-home, cross-activity, cross-task) work automatically once opted in; in-app animations need Navigation/Compose Material support."

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Callbacks register with OnBackInvokedDispatcher (API 33+; compat via AndroidX Activity 1.6+). The dispatcher is callback-based before the gesture starts: the system must know before the gesture whether the app will handle back, hence onBackPressed overrides can't work. Flags: Android 15 enables the back-to-home animation as default for apps that opt in; verify developer-option vs default behaviour per API level. PredictiveBackHandler { progress -> try { progress.collect { /* animate */ } ; commit() } catch (e: CancellationException) { reset() } }.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
var scale by remember { mutableFloatStateOf(1f) }
PredictiveBackHandler(enabled = canGoBack) { progress ->
    try {
        progress.collect { e -> scale = 1f - 0.1f * e.progress }
        navigateBack()
    } catch (e: CancellationException) { scale = 1f; throw e }
}

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Still overriding onBackPressed(): not called under predictive back.
  • Calling finish() in a callback that was enabled conditionally late: gesture preview already committed to system.
  • Enabling BackHandler(enabled=true) always, which swallows the system back-to-home animation.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Why must the handler be enabled ahead of time? → The system decides animation type up front.
  2. How is it different from BackHandler? → BackHandler is a commit-only callback; PredictiveBackHandler exposes progress.
  3. Navigation-compose? → Newer versions animate destination transitions by progress (verify version).

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE: add manifest flag. Senior: explains pre-registered callback model, cancellation semantics, and not swallowing system transitions.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A modal bottom sheet's custom back logic via onKeyDown stopped working after opt-in; users could not dismiss it by back.

questions.contextHtml:
After targeting SDK 35, QA reports on a Pixel with 3-button navigation the bottom tab bar is half hidden, and on gesture nav the "Continue" button text touches the gesture pill. Code:

Scaffold(
    bottomBar = { BottomBar() }
) { padding ->
    Column(Modifier.fillMaxSize()) {
        Header()
        Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f))
        Button(onClick = {}, Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(16.dp)) { Text("Continue") }
    }
}

BottomBar is a Material NavigationBar. The Header looks fine. Crash rate is unchanged; only 2% of tickets, all with 3-button nav.
questions.promptHtml: Find the bug(s) and fix them.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Add 48dp bottom padding." That hardcodes a value that is wrong on gesture nav, landscape and tablets.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Nav mode of the affected devices (3-button vs gesture)? Does the Scaffold have contentWindowInsets customised? Is enableEdgeToEdge() called? Are there sibling screens with the same pattern?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Not an incident; merge a patch fix and ship in the next train. If severe, a server flag is not applicable.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) Scaffold's padding is ignored (the lambda param is unused), so content isn't inset; (b) NavigationBar handles its own insets so it should be fine, but is clipped when nested under another padded parent; (c) enableEdgeToEdge() missing so bars are opaque on some OEMs. Red herring: 3-button vs gesture merely changes inset size.
  4. How I'd verify each: Layout Inspector with insets overlay, compile warning "unused parameter padding" (Compose lint UnusedMaterial3ScaffoldPaddingParameter), preview with DeviceConfigurationOverride.WindowInsets (ui-test, Compose 1.8+, verify) or emulator with 3-button nav.
  5. Root cause: padding from Scaffold is not applied to the content: content fills the whole window and draws under the top bar/bottom bar region. The button lands in the bar's area, partly hidden/overlapping.
  6. Fix:
Scaffold(bottomBar = { BottomBar() }) { padding ->
    Column(Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(padding).consumeWindowInsets(padding)) {
        Header(); Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f))
        Button(onClick = {}, Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(16.dp)) { Text("Continue") }
    }
}
  1. Prevention: Keep the UnusedMaterial3ScaffoldPaddingParameter lint as error; add screenshot tests with 3-button and gesture insets; review checklist for insets.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: No hardcoded dp. No systemBarsPadding() on top of Scaffold (double-apply, see Q340).

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Why did gesture nav look "OK"? → Gesture bar inset is small (~24dp), button's 16dp margin almost covers it.
  • What if the button must float above the keyboard? → consumeWindowInsets(padding).imePadding().
  • Landscape cutout? → Scaffold's default insets include display cutout horizontally for content (verify).

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A release passed QA on gesture-only devices; the first 3-button user ticket came from the CEO's phone. Since then screenshot tests run with both nav modes.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: hardcodes dp or can't find the unused parameter.
  • Hire: applies padding and explains why.
  • Strong hire: adds consumption, lint, insets-aware screenshot testing.

questions.contextHtml: Release 8.4 targets SDK 35. 18% of login sessions on Android 15 devices abandon at the password step; support says "keyboard covers the button" and others report "huge gap above keyboard". Crash rate flat. Code: Scaffold with contentWindowInsets = WindowInsets(0), content Column(Modifier.padding(inner).imePadding().verticalScroll(..)). Manifest has adjustPan. Android 14 is fine. 2.1M DAU on Android 15.
questions.promptHtml: Diagnose and ship a fix within a day.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Switch to adjustResize." That may help the cover but not the gap, and ignores edge-to-edge changes in the insets model.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Which devices report the gap (gesture or 3-button)? Which window mode? Is the screen a Dialog/BottomSheet? When did abandonment start relative to the targetSdk rollout? Does the issue repro with the Google keyboard vs OEM keyboards?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Halt staged rollout at the current percentage; ship a hotfix to the form screen only; remote config can't fix layout, but can swap login to a web-view fallback if one exists.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) adjustPan conflicts with explicit imePadding: the window pans and also pads, so the gap and the covering coexist; (b) nav-bar inset applied twice (inner + ime); (c) OEM keyboard reports different IME inset; (d) red herring: Compose version.
  4. How I'd verify each: Repro on Android 15 emulator with gesture and 3-button; Layout Inspector "show insets"; log WindowInsets.ime.getBottom(density) and navigationBars from Modifier.onSizeChanged; toggle adjustResize.
  5. Root cause: With edge-to-edge enforced, the system no longer resizes the window with adjustResize semantics the old fitsSystemWindows code relied on, and adjustPan pans the window by the focused field while imePadding also grows padding, so content shifts twice. The WindowInsets(0) scaffold removed bar insets, but IME inset still includes the nav-bar height (the IME inset overlaps navigation bar), causing the gap since nav-bar inset isn't consumed.
  6. Fix: Set windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize"; use the pattern Modifier.padding(inner).consumeWindowInsets(inner).imePadding() with Scaffold contentWindowInsets = WindowInsets.safeDrawing.exclude(WindowInsets.ime) default behaviour. Long-term: shared FormScaffold composable with screenshot tests.
  7. Prevention: Instrumented test with WindowInsetsAnimation-independent harness (set insets via ui-test override), staged rollout gating on login completion rate, lint for adjustPan + imePadding.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not reverting targetSdk (Play deadline). Not hardcoding gap offsets per OEM.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Fix works but jumpy on API 29? → No animated insets before 30; accept a step, or use adjustResize fallback.
  • Dialog-based login? → Dialog window needs its own imePadding, platform dialogs don't inherit.
  • What if the field is in a LazyColumn? → bringIntoViewRequester on focus plus imeNestedScroll.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A funnel dashboard showed a cliff only on one OS version; the team initially blamed the SMS provider. Splitting funnels by OS version plus nav mode found it in an hour.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: toggles manifest flags randomly.
  • Hire: identifies adjustPan + imePadding double handling and consumption.
  • Strong hire: also halts rollout, adds an inset test harness and funnel monitoring.

questions.contextHtml: You own a portrait-locked retail app (screenOrientation="portrait", resizeableActivity="false"). 9% of 4M MAU are on tablets/foldables/ChromeOS (sw >= 600dp). Plan is to target API 36 in 8 weeks. Play Console large-screen quality warnings exist. QA found the camera scan screen crops and the cart screen stretches fields to 1100dp width.
questions.promptHtml: How do you migrate safely without a big-bang rewrite?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Use the opt-out property and delay." It's temporary; the table says API 37 won't allow it (verify).

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Which screens are highest-traffic on large screens? Are there camera/sensor flows? Is there a design system with max-width tokens? What is the acceptable launch bar (functional vs polished)?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Ship the target-36 build with the temporary compat opt-out property on tablets only for screens not ready, per-activity if possible; add analytics for window size class.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: Biggest risks: scanner preview transforms, hardcoded dimension assumptions, state loss on resize, dialogs/bottom sheets full-width, tests that assume portrait.
  4. How I'd verify each: Resizable emulator, window-size sweeps in screenshot tests (compact/medium/expanded), Macrobenchmark on tablet AVD, Play pre-launch device lab for large screen.
  5. Root cause: Locking was a design shortcut; Android 16 ignores it so every layout is exposed.
  6. Fix: Phase 1: container max-width (widthIn(max=600.dp) centered) as safe baseline; Phase 2: NavigationSuiteScaffold and list-detail on key flows; Phase 3: camera rotation using window rotation. Remove manifest locks last, behind release train.
  7. Prevention: CI screenshot matrix with size classes; lint check on screenOrientation; add device tiers to release dashboard.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not shipping full tablet redesign before the deadline; not leaving the opt-out until API 37.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Product wants phone to remain portrait-only? → Allowed: phones (<600dp) still honour the lock.
  • Scanner is inconsistent on ChromeOS? → Use CameraX with ViewPort and window rotation; test camera orientation sensors.
  • How to measure success? → Large-screen crash/ANR rate, session length, Play quality tier.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A team used the opt-out, forgot it, and discovered at the next target bump that 40 screens had never been resized.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: relies on the opt-out.
  • Hire: phased plan with max-width baseline and testing.
  • Strong hire: adds measurement, sunset tracking, camera/state specifics.

questions.contextHtml: A note-taking app shows 1.8% crash-free regression on Galaxy Fold devices (~120k users). Stack: IllegalStateException: Fragment already added after unfolding; also users lose the half-typed note. Activity declares configChanges="orientation|screenSize" only; the inner display change also flips smallestScreenSize and screenLayout. Logcat shows Activity recreated after unfold.
questions.promptHtml: Why does this happen and how do you fix it?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Catch the exception." Hides the loss of state and doesn't address recreation.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Does the crash occur only on fold events? Fragment transactions in onCreate? Is the note draft in a ViewModel or in a View?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Add smallestScreenSize|screenLayout to configChanges as a hotfix; save drafts to Room debounced.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) missing configChanges flags cause recreation on fold; (b) fragment added unconditionally in onCreate without a savedInstanceState == null check; (c) draft in a non-saved remember.
  4. How I'd verify each: Foldable emulator with virtual hinge; adb shell dumpsys activity for config; log onSaveInstanceState.
  5. Root cause: Unfold changes smallestScreenSize/screenLayout, not covered, so recreate; the activity re-adds fragments the FragmentManager already restored.
  6. Fix: List full flags; guard if (savedInstanceState == null); drafts in ViewModel with SavedStateHandle; adaptive layout reacts to size class.
  7. Prevention: Fold-event instrumented test via WindowLayoutInfoPublisherRule; recreate test with ActivityScenario.recreate().
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not relying only on configChanges: recreation can still occur (process death, other changes), so state must survive both.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Why not remove configChanges? → Recreation is correct if state survives, but expensive (media/camera).
  • Process death while folded? → SavedStateHandle/Room restore.
  • Tabletop switching? → Not a config change in all cases; WindowInfoTracker events.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: The first reproduction came from a QA engineer folding a phone during a demo, not from any test.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: catches exception.
  • Hire: finds configChanges gap and guards fragment add.
  • Strong hire: adds fold test, state durability, and drafts in storage.

questions.contextHtml: Product says: "Make the video player great on foldables." No other detail. Player is Compose + Media3, 600k MAU, 3% foldable users. You have 2 weeks and one test device.
questions.promptHtml: How do you turn this into a shippable plan?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: Starts building a custom hinge layout immediately without defining scope or success.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Which postures matter (tabletop, book, flat unfolded)? Is the gain engagement or quality bar? Do we support PiP/multi-window? What's the minimum fold devices to certify?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Not an incident; deliver in slices: (1) correct resize/unfold without restart, (2) tabletop layout, (3) polish.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: Value is highest in tabletop (video above fold, controls below), then large unfolded window.
  4. How I'd verify each: Foldable emulator with hinge sensors, WindowInfoTracker test publisher, one real device, instrumented playback continuity test (position preserved across fold).
  5. Root cause: Requirement is vague; playback state must be independent of layout.
  6. Fix: Player state in ViewModel/Service; layout switch on FoldingFeature HALF_OPENED + HORIZONTAL; controls panel anchored below bounds.bottom.
  7. Prevention: Feature flag, analytics on posture usage.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Skip book-mode custom UI v1; do not target OEM-specific SDKs.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Device without hinge occlusion? → use fold bounds if present, else 50/50 only when isSeparating.
  • Posture flapping while hand-held? → debounce 150-300 ms (tune).
  • Cover display? → Treated as a separate small window; ensure resize works.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A "foldable support" ticket without acceptance criteria took a quarter; restating it as three measurable slices shipped the first in a week.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: starts coding.
  • Hire: clarifies, slices, uses WindowManager.
  • Strong hire: defines metrics, feature flag, state independence.

questions.contextHtml: Team debates: A) one codebase with size-class-driven composables; B) separate phone/ and tablet/ navigation graphs with different screens. App has 60 screens, 25 engineers, tablets are 6% of DAU but 14% of revenue. Release cadence is biweekly.
questions.promptHtml: Which do you choose and what guardrails?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "A, because DRY." Ignores divergence cost when tablet UX genuinely differs.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: How different is tablet UX (rail + list-detail vs same flows)? Who owns tablet design? Can analytics show tablet task completion? Is multi-window/ChromeOS in scope?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Start with A for shared screens; carve out a few screens (inbox, checkout) with dedicated expanded variants.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: Single graph with adaptive scaffolds covers 80% of screens; a few deserve distinct composables behind the same ViewModel/state contract.
  4. How I'd verify each: Screenshot matrix across sizes, tablet-specific revenue funnels, app size/build time comparisons.
  5. Root cause: Window size not device type is the right axis since the same device changes class (split-screen, fold).
  6. Fix: Shared ViewModels and UI state; screen-level when (sizeClass) choosing a layout composable; navigation via one NavHost with adaptive scaffolds.
  7. Prevention: Design-system tokens (max content width, grid), CI screenshot tests for 3 classes.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not separate graphs per device type (state loss on resize, duplicated logic); not hiding features on larger windows.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Tablet design team wants unique flows? → allowed if the ViewModel contract is shared.
  • Perf on low-end tablets? → lazy layouts, avoid composing both variants at once.
  • Test explosion? → size-class parameterised screenshot tests with sampled screens.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A dual-graph app lost the user's cart whenever a tablet user entered split-screen, as the activity switched graphs.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: picks by preference.
  • Hire: window-based approach with shared state.
  • Strong hire: adds data (revenue), guardrails, selective divergence.

questions.contextHtml: ChromeOS reviews (4% of installs, 2.9 stars vs 4.5 phone) complain: "can't use keyboard Tab", "right-click does nothing", "window can't be resized properly", "scroll with wheel is slow". A Compose app with many clickables and custom pointerInput for gestures. The team has 1 sprint and one Chromebook.
questions.promptHtml: What do you fix first and how do you test without a farm of devices?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Not our target." Large-screen quality increasingly affects Play visibility.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Which reviews map to which root cause (focus, mouse events, resizing)? Can we get ChromeOS device share and revenue? Is Play large-screen tiering visible?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Ship quick wins: ensure resizeableActivity=true, fix configChanges, enable keyboard focus handling.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) custom pointerInput ignores mouse-specific events (hover, secondary click, scroll); (b) focus order not defined, no focus indicators; (c) fixed-size window; (d) wheel scroll speed is system behaviour, check it's the standard scrollable not custom.
  4. How I'd verify each: Resizable emulator + ChromeOS Android emulator image (Android Studio), hardware keyboard in emulator; Compose semantics tests with performKeyInput/performMouseInput; Accessibility Scanner for focus.
  5. Root cause: Touch-only assumptions.
  6. Fix: Use clickable/focusable (focus + Enter/Space free), Modifier.onKeyEvent for shortcuts (Ctrl+F, Ctrl+N), combinedClickable + onPointerEvent for secondary click and hover, PointerEventType.Scroll handling when custom; keep standard verticalScroll/lazy for wheel.
  7. Prevention: Add Chromebook smoke test (resizable AVD) to release checklist; track large-screen quality in Play Console.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: No ChromeOS-only code paths; keep input generic across mouse/stylus/keyboard.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Stylus? → PointerType.Stylus and MotionEvent pressure/tilt, palm rejection via system.
  • Hover tooltips? → TooltipBox / hover modifiers.
  • Test on emulator enough? → Use real device before release for input latency and window management.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: Adding Tab-focus and Enter handling to forms moved ChromeOS rating from 2.9 to 3.8 in two releases with no visual change.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: dismisses.
  • Hire: identifies input gaps and uses standard modifiers.
  • Strong hire: gives a test strategy, metrics, and limits of emulation.
